## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 82, titled *Anuvassa* ("Ordaining every year"), establishes a rule concerning the frequency with which a nun may confer ordination: a nun who ordains candidates in consecutive years commits an offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral]. The background story (*vatthu*) explains that when nuns admitted probationers (*sikkhamānā*s) into the order every year, living quarters were insufficient (*upassaya tath' eva na sammati / vasanokāso na ppahoti*) [Hüsken 1997]. Under the disciplinary framework, a nun acting as a preceptor (*pavattinī*) is restricted to conducting ordinations only every two years rather than annually [Hüsken 1997]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Full parallels recorded by SuttaCentral occur throughout the Vinaya traditions of multiple schools: the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 138*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 118*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 126*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 124; Tibetan Pc 84), Mahāsāṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 106*), and Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc106*) [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus detects extensive text reuse across 97 texts, showing the closest structural parallels with adjacent Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules, most notably Pācittiya 83 (sharing §1.1–2.2.5), Pācittiya 61, Pācittiya 74, and Pācittiya 62 [DharmaNexus]. Ute Hüsken similarly observes that the narrative framing of Pācittiya 82 is closely paralleled in Pācittiya 83 [Hüsken 1997].
